In late October, Questing Goose Studio and publisher tinyBuild presented Probably Stolen - Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim. It is a cyberpunk merchant simulator in which players are invited to build a business on a massive space station “divided by wealth and corruption”.

A few days later, the developers announced that game sales had surpassed 500,000 copies. At a certain point, the game reached 12th place on the Steam sales chart — while Cyberpunk 2077 held 11th. This weekend, Probably Stolen climbed to 7th place, while Cyberpunk 2077 dropped to 23rd.

1 / 2 Image source: SteamDB website The protagonist of Probably Stolen - Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is a former scavenger who managed to open a small shop thanks to a loan: “Now rent is rising, various factions are watching your every move, and most of your profits come from working in the ‘gray zones’ of what is considered legal.”

Reviews for Probably Stolen - Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim on Steam are “Overwhelmingly Positive” — holding a 96% rating after more than 6,000 user reviews.

items.content: Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated title, Grand Theft Auto 6, is scheduled to release on November 19, 2026. With only a few months left until the game’s release, October could be the perfect time to catch up on some of the open-world games you may have missed—or revisit a few classics before Rockstar’s GTA 6 eventually takes over your free time. More like this GTA’s Strangest Myths: A Full History If you are looking for games that deliver a similar classic open-world experience and should be must-plays before GTA 6, then Rockstar Games’ Red Dead Redemption 2, Cyberpunk 2077, Mafia: The Old Country, previous GTA titles like GTA 5 and GTA 4, should be on your list. Starting with one of Rockstar’s own open-world classics, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a great place to begin.

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

items.title: Check out what's coming to Cyberpunk 2077 in the Edgerunners 2 Update!
items.summary: Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you! Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watc
items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.summary: You might want to get on board.

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter If you're a fan of CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, you might have been excited about some of the headlines appearing in the past couple of days. 'New Cyberpunk 2077 game reveals official gameplay,' one read. ‘Cyberpunk 2077 returns with ambitious new release,' was another. One even suggested that a new Cyberpunk 2077 was going to steal GTA 6's thunder.

Alas, some fans might have been disappointed to read those stories and discover that the new game is more analogue than what they might have imagined. Given how long it takes to make an AAA video game, it was highly unlikely that we would get Cyberpunk 2077 2 in 2027 – 2028 maybe, but even that's a very optimistic estimate.

The new Cyberpunk 2077 is, in fact, a board game. But don't write it off, it follows in a long traditional of video game to board game transitions, and some of them have been quite good.

Watch On Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game looks set to do justice to the video game's vast lore and worldbuilding in its physical scale. The eight-minute unboxing video above reveals just how huge it is with the various miniatures, mission cards, character boards and gameplay expansions

Published by Go On Board, it's billed as a cooperative, story-driven campaign game. Players take on the roles of Edgerunners, exploring Night City and completing 13 multi-stage missions. A timer mechanic is intended to replicate the paced of the action of the video game.

Dispatch's new Deluxe Edition lets you play the whole game as storyboard animatics GTA 6's leak exposes the uncomfortable truth about digital-only games Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival is the horror game AAA publishers have been too prudish to make The game follows the release of the trading card game Cyberpunk TCG. If its successful, it should be able to evolve alongside the video game franchise for many years.

The trend of turning video games into board games has exploded over the past decade, with crowdfunding platforms like Kickstarter or Gamefound playing a big role in helping the physical adaptations get off the ground. They also tap into the growing interest in physical media and analogue tech as a respite from digital screen time, providing a physical social experience.

Critical reception has been a bit of a mixed bag. Some have been heralded as masterpieces, others are criticised as overpriced miniature-fests that prioritise plastic over playable design.

The most successful adaptations are those that don't just copy-paste the digital game, but translate its feeling and core loops into smart, physical mechanics. Slay the Spire: The Board Game is much loved for how it turned a single-player digital roguelike and turning it into cooperative tabletop deck-builder, and Frostpunk succeeded in bringing the punishing decision-making of digital survival games to the table.

On a very different note, the cosy Dorfromantik: The Board Game captured the zen-like puzzle game vibe of its digital counterpart.

The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past's lush new location and remaster improvements have me excited to be Geralt again GTA 6 will “raise the bar” by ignoring game industry trends, says Helldivers 2 dev The secret to Stuntman: Hollywood’s success is Hollywood itself On the other hand, Dark Souls: The Board Game was seen by some as being tedious and repetitive despite its gorgeous miniatures.

Board games can also be the ultimate collector's item for video game fans. Even if a $200 Elden Ring or Resident Evil board games only hits the table once or twice a year, the gorgeous, highly detailed miniatures also serve as display pieces.

You can find out more about Cyberpunk 2077 The Board Game on the Go On Board website.

items.summary: Opinion | The grind is worth it – and finally, so is the Game Pass Ultimate price tag
items.content:
Opinion | The grind is worth it – and finally, so is the Game Pass Ultimate price tag

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those weird yet wonderful RPGs that, unless you've come prepared, seems to fight you at every turn. I'm not talking about the Tyger Claws running rampant on the streets of Japantown; rather, the mechanics themselves are a lot to wrap one's head around as a Night City newbie.

I first stepped into CD Projekt Red 's thrilling open-world in 2024. A couple of weeks later, I ended up dropping it entirely for two months. There was nothing wrong with the game itself – I'd picked it up alongside then-new DLC Phantom Liberty, with Patch 2.1 very much intact – but something about it pushed back against my every attempt to fall in love.

Fast forward to 2026, and I called Cyberpunk 2077 the best RPG of all time, no exceptions. I thrive on a challenge, and that is precisely what Night City presented me with. It just so happens that challenging games are what Xbox Game Pass needs more of if Microsoft wants to justify that ever-climbing price tag – which is why I need you to give Cyberpunk, which is now on Game Pass, a shot.

After 700 hours, Cyberpunk 2077 has unexpectedly become one of my comfort RPGs

Grind is life in some games, but a good game should not come with a reading list. No one should have to research the best builds for a given playstyle, or watch endless explainers to suss out an RPG system – not immediately, anyway. That's one area where, despite how much I love the overall experience, Cyberpunk 2077 falters.

I've mentioned in the past how Night City throwing you into the deep end resonates with the overwhelming muchness of life in the city. Everything is familiar yet alien in this dystopian future. If that just applied to worldbuilding itself, that would be one thing. But I had no idea how cyberware, crafting, Sandevistans, or the skill trees themselves truly worked or synergized until about halfway through the RPG. Nothing is explained, and very little is inferred. I pondered whether that is because so many returning players will have hopped back in (warily, most likely) following Cyberpunk's super buggy initial 2020 launch, but after reading up on how much of the game's systems have changed in the last 6 years, the lack of even basic signposting still strikes me as strange.

After over 1000 in Cyberpunk 2077, I'm convinced the Nomads are the best group and lifepath Cyberpunk 2077 dev doesn't think Phantom Liberty's success "erases" the launch of the base game Cyberpunk 2077's new update just made it the anti-GTA 6

But therein lies the fun. For me, at least, having to prove myself to the game was incredibly satisfying. My two-month break was predominantly occupied by Gamescom 2024 prep, and once I'd cleared my plate of Work Games, I could return to a Fun Personal Challenge. That challenge was partly fueled by a refusal to have wasted £80 on a game I would never play, I'll admit. But it's also just how my brain works. I love to prove others wrong, and that includes myself.

Before long, I was able to lock into the game and stop fighting back. Instead, I used my damn brain for a change – and reminded myself how, since this is a CDPR game, it was bound to come with layers of lore-intensive systems to unpick. I had a similar issue with The Witcher 3's mutagen systems . If I could work out what to do with my many-colored monster samples, surely I could conquer a few bits of tech in Cyberpunk 2077?

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

I hope this move means that Microsoft is keen to bring more time-intensive experiences to Game Pass

The grind was worth it. I ended up playing four complete Cyberpunk playthroughs one after the other, utterly spellbound by the story, the place, and the characters I'd come to love so much. That makes it one of the best value for money games I've ever picked up, right alongside Baldur's Gate 3 .

items.title: New Cyberpunk 2077 Game Officially Announced
items.summary: A brand-new Cyberpunk game has been revealed, but it might not be what fans expect.
items.content:
Image via CD Projekt Red Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Mandi Odoerfer Published Jan 24, 2026, 10:00 PM EST Mandi has been writing about comics and video games for more than ten years and has been reading and playing them her entire life. Her writing has been featured at TapTap , GameZone , US Gamer, and many other sites. She joined CBR in 2024, where she works as a writer and editor, covering video games and comic books. In her downtime, she occasionally muses about anime, RPGs, and the best Steam demos on her Substack, Cartoon Ghost , though she often finds herself retreating to the comfort of her favorite games. Mandi is currently replaying the entire Pokémon series, starting with Red & Blue . Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 5 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Cyberpunk 2077 had a rocky launch, but it's completely turned things around since then, becoming one of the greatest open-world games of all time. Now, a brand-new Cyberpunk 2077 game is on the way, but it might not be what fans expect.

WeirdCo, a Seattle-based trading card company, has announced a new Cyberpunk 2077 TCG. The planned game is officially licensed and will feature fan-favorite characters from the Cyberpunk franchise.

Like the hit open-world RPG, the upcoming Cyberpunk 2077 trading game is set in Night City, a neon metropolis plagued by corruption. Players will build decks and create an edgerunning crew, battling opponents and taking on gigs to build a reputation.

Gaining reputation will give players access to high-level gigs, along with more powerful tools and abilities. That means players will have to stay one step ahead of their opponents if they don't want to be left behind.

A recent livestream showed off the full gameplay loop, giving players a taste of what it'll be like to play the actual game. It looks like it'll be an incredibly dynamic card game that will appeal to fans of the Cyberpunk 2077 franchise and TCG and tabletop fans alike.

Cards featuring popular characters like V and Judy Alvarez have already been revealed, and more cards will be shown soon. A Kickstarter campaign for the card game is set to launch on March 17, 2026.

cyberpunk 2077 original promo asset Image via CD Projekt RED After five years, Cyberpunk 2077 is closing the book on some chapters and opening new ones. Recently, the game's creative director, Igor Sarzynski, confirmed that there were no plans to extend the game's opening act , an update that had been highly requested by fans.

"Would extending Act 1 (before the heist) in CP77 make the game better? No, it wouldn't," said Sarzynski. "It's like saying we should spend more time on Tatooine with farmer Luke before he got involved with all this Jedi stuff."

He also assured fans that content from a longer opening hadn't been cut from the game. "No, half-year montage is not cut content. We always planned it like this."

A sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 , Cyberpunk 2 , entered pre-development in 2025, but it's still a long way off. CD Projekt has said that the game may not release until 2030, stating "our journey from pre-production to final release takes four to five years on average."

Fans will have to wait a long time for the next Cyberpunk 2077 video game, and since there are no more expansions planned for the game, it'll be years before they get new content in that universe. The upcoming Cyberpunk TCG might make that brutal wait a little bit easier to manage.

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
